verdict.rationale: Sentry's API is explicitly versioned: the docs say "the current version of the Sentry's web API is considered v0", and the official OpenAPI schema covers the /api/0/ surface. A dedicated API Deprecation Policy is published on getsentry's developer site. Reliability is weaker than the story implies: v0 is described as "still under development", beta endpoints are "subject to change", and the policy is engineering-facing documentation rather than a customer-facing contract. Missing for 10: a stable post-v0 versioned API with compatibility guarantees, a customer-facing deprecation contract with documented notice periods, and independent corroboration that deprecations are handled as the policy describes.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: The current version of the Sentry's web API is considered v0. Our public endpoints are generally stable, but beta endpoints are subject to change.
Sentry publishes a dedicated API Deprecation Policy on its developer-documentation site (develop.sentry.dev, getsentry-owned), governing how public endpoints are deprecated.

The official getsentry/sentry-api-schema repository publishes the dereferenced OpenAPI 3.0.3 document for the "Sentry Public API" (info title "API Reference", version v0), covering the full /api/0/ surface.
